newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Carpetright upbeat on sales outlook.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Carpetright upbeat on sales outlook.

text.p: British carpet and floorcoverings retailer Carpetright Plc sent its shares soaring on Tuesday with a 28 percent increase in annual profits and a recovery in sales since May.
Chairman and chief executive Lord Harris said the group was confident about prospects now there were signs of a recovery in sales after a slack period early in the year.
Harris said, "With a prosperous economy and an improving housing market, we are confident of further market progress over the next 12 months."

The group, which has grown rapidly over the past nine years into a chain of more than 200 stores, boosted sales by 26 percent to 233.9 million pounds ($382.7 million), and increased its dividend by 31 percent to 19.0 pence a share.
Pretax profits rose 28 percent to 32.2 million pounds, in line with market forecasts.
Sales were helped by a slightly stronger market, but trading conditions weakened in the run up to Britain's general election on May 1.
Harris said the carpet market was showing signs of recovering after slackening off sharply early in the year.
In calendar 1996 the overall market was up by five percent, he said, but in the first four months of 1997 it dropped by 10 percent.

He said the market had slowed down sharply before the last three general elections, and this year was no exception. Other retailers have found that consumers put off making purchases ahead of the election, but consumer confidence shot up immediately afterwards.
Harris said things were now picking up and the group had seen a four percent increase in comparable store sales in the seven weeks since the beginning of May.
"We're feeling the recovery already," Harris told Reuters.
The current sales trend spurred a rally in the shares, which had been depressed ahead of the results. They stood 39.5 pence higher at 480.5 pence each.
"The results were as expected but they had a good outlook and their sales have done well in the last couple of months," one market-maker said.
The group increased market share last year to about 17 percent from 13 and aims to take 30 percent of the market over time, vying for top slot with rival Allied Carpets Plc.

Harris said the recovery in the market in the past few weeks suggested carpets might take some of the windfall cash flowing to consumers from the demutualisation of building societies such as Halifax and Alliance and Leicester.
"The last couple of weeks have been picking up, there's a bit of evidence," he said.

Capital expenditure last year was 32.5 million pounds, up from 22 million in the previous year. This year Harris estimated capital spending would be lower at around 14 million pounds, because of fewer opportunities to buy freehold sites.
The firm has 210 Carpetright stores and plans to open 20 more in the next year. It's longer term aim is for 260 Carpetrights in mainland Britain, plus 10 in Northern Ireland.

Harris was confident about prospects for the group's new more upmarket Carpet Depot format, which could eventually have 120 "showroom-only" stores and 120 superstores across Britain. It had 57 stores at the end of April and there are plans for about 20 more this year.
The Harris family holds a 20 percent stake in the company, which he founded. In January he sold four million of his shares. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
